gloss: to sit down; to take a seat

definitions.gloss: to sit down; to take a seat; to settle down
definitions.explanation: To lower oneself into a sitting position. More literary or deliberate than {座|すわ}る, often implying carefully or comfortably settling into a seat.

examples.japanese: ベンチに{腰|こし}を{下|お}ろした。
examples.english: I sat down on a bench.

examples.japanese: どうぞ、そちらに{腰|こし}を{下|お}ろしてください。
examples.english: Please, have a seat over there.

examples.japanese: {疲|つか}れたので、{木陰|こかげ}に{腰|こし}を{下|お}ろして{休憩|きゅうけい}した。
examples.english: I was tired, so I sat down in the shade of a tree and took a break.

notes:
USAGE:
The verb {下|お}ろす conjugates normally as a godan verb. This expression is more descriptive and slightly more formal or literary than simply {座|すわ}る (to sit). It draws attention to the physical action of lowering oneself.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～に{腰|こし}を{下|お}ろす (to sit down on/at ~)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {座|すわ}る is the everyday word for sitting down
- {腰|こし}を{下|お}ろす emphasizes the deliberate act of settling into a seat, often used in narrative writing
- {腰|こし}を{掛|か}ける is a similar expression, slightly more formal
